compiled_state.title: As a /dso:review orchestrator, my tier upgrade decisions depend only on explicit ESCALATE_REVIEW signals, not on cycle-attempt count
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Remove the PASS_NUM>=2 light->standard ratchet and the MAX_ATTEMPTS->deep upgrade from REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md (anchor: conditional `if [ "${REVIEW_PASS_NUM}" -ge 2 ]` and post-loop block following 'MAX_ATTEMPTS exceeded'). Review REVIEW-WORKFLOW-HUGE.md FALLBACK for ratchet patterns; remove or document divergence. Add short-circuit oscillation detection: 2 consecutive proximity-repeat NEW_INTRODUCED in same file+region without escape_rationale → ESCALATE_REVIEW: oscillation_no_arbiter_engagement. Also fire on MAX_ATTEMPTS exhaustion without any arbiter dispatch.
**Why**: SC5 tier decoupling. Each tier upgrade is a fresh stateless review that surfaces new findings; removing cycle-count ratchets eliminates a major cycle-bloat source.
**Scope**:
  IN:
  - PASS_NUM>=2 ratchet removed from REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md
  - MAX_ATTEMPTS->deep upgrade removed
  - REVIEW-WORKFLOW-HUGE.md FALLBACK reviewed and updated (or divergence documented)
  - Short-circuit oscillation detection on proximity-repeat NEW_INTRODUCED across 2 cycles
  - MAX_ATTEMPTS exhaustion without arbiter dispatch fires ESCALATE_REVIEW: oscillation_no_arbiter_engagement (covers red team #11)
  - Regression test: tier stays at initial value across 2+ resolution cycles with no ESCALATE_REVIEW signal; ast-grep/grep scan confirms ratchet logic absent
  OUT:
  - Arbiter dispatch (S10)
  - Proximity verification (S9)

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, tier upgrades only fire on explicit ESCALATE_REVIEW from the resolution sub-agent; the cycle-count ratchets are absent from the workflow files
  ← Satisfies: "Tier upgrade decoupled from cycle-attempt count, including HUGE workflow and short-circuit oscillation detection"
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic

## Considerations

- [Reliability] MAX_ATTEMPTS retained as backstop with new ESCALATE_REVIEW exit path covering the non-proximity oscillation case

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
